Name: Double integrals/Dubbelintegraler
Basic relationship:
The limit of the sum of inscribed or circumscribed prisms with base \D A = \D x \D y equals the volume under the surface z = f(x,y) and is given by the double integral between (x_1, x_2) and (y_1, y_2) [Image]

lim{n->\infty, \S{i=1, n, f(x_i, y_i)*\D A_i}} = int2{D, f(x, y)dxdy} = int{x_1, x_2, int{y_1, y_2, f(x,y) dy} dx}

Basic relationship:
int2{D, f(x, y)dxdy} = int{E, f(x(u, v), y(u, v))|\\d(x, y)/\\d(u, v)|dudv}, |\\d(x, y)/\\d(u, v)| = det|[[\\dx/\\du, \\dx/\\dv], [\\dy/\\du, \\dy/\\dv]]|
det|[[\\dx/\\du, \\dx/\\dv, \\dx/\\dw], [\\dy/\\du, \\dy/\\dv, \\dy/\\dw], [\\dz/\\du, \\dz/\\dv, \\dz/\\dw]]|
(x=x(u, v), y=y(u, v))

similar to int{f(x)dx} = int{f(g(u))g'(u)du}
du->0, g(u+du) = g(u) + g'(u)du

x(r, \t) = r*cos(\t)

Name: TRIPLE INTEGRALS/Trippelintegraler
Basic relationship:
Triple integrals are three-dimensional extensions of double integrals defined in analogous fashion [Image]

lim{n->\inf, \S{i=1, n, f(x_i, y_i, z_i)*\D V_i} = int{x_1, x_2, int{y_1, y_2, int{z_1, z_2, f(x,y,z) dz} dy} dx}

Presetted values:
K = {(x, y, z): x+y+z<=1, x>=0, y>=0, z>=0}
int3{K, y*dV} = int3{K, y*dxdydz} = int{0, 1, int{0, 1-x, int{0, 1-x-y, y*dz}dy}dx}

Name: ITERATED & PARTIAL INTEGRALS
Area of a curved surface
Presetted values:
Find the area in the first octant cut from the cylindrical surface z = 4 - x^2 by the plane y = x.

Since boundaries of projection of the required area onto the x-y plane are y = 0, y = x, and x = 2, we have A = int{0, 2, int{0, x, sqrt(1 + (dz/dx)^2 + (dz/dy)^2) dydx}} = int{0, 2, int{0, x, sqrt(1 + 4x^2 + 0) dydx}}, A = int{0, 2, sqrt(1 + 4x^2) x dx} = (1/12)*(17*sqrt(17) - 1)

This result can also be found, though with much greater difficulty, by reversing the order of integration:
A = int{0, 2, int{y, 2, sqrt(1 + 4x^2 + 0) dxdy}}
Thus, ease of evaluation often depends on order of integration
